intended_object: A canonical isomorphism between the degree-(n+1) homology of the complex of global sections of the functorial flasque (Godement-type) resolution of a sheaf F and the cokernel of the map on global sections F_n(X) → C(F_n)(X), where F_n is the n-th iterated flasque-envelope quotient. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in FlasqueResolution.lean (lines 836, 848).
explanation: This is not a mathematical object. It is a `def` only because its value is data (an isomorphism, `≅`), and it plays the role of a lemma. It composes Mathlib's `homologyIsoSc'` with the library's own `flasqueResolutionSectionsHomologyIsoCokernel`, so that the homology of the whole complex can be written as a concrete cokernel. The library then uses it (lines 836 and 848) to compare its flasque-resolution cohomology with other constructions. Such a bookkeeping isomorphism inside a proof has no standalone counterpart in the literature that it should match. The docstring's claim, that the homology in degree n+1 is this cokernel, is what the body builds. So nothing here is incorrect or too narrow; the restriction to `TopCat.{0}` belongs to the surrounding development, not to this definition.
